A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LinMU and provide readable text, equations, algorithms, figures and tables that can be reliably matched. Full-document inspection finds no appendices in either supplied PDF.

before.justification: v1 reports original distillation experiments, benchmark scores, inference measurements and ablations for NVILA-based and Qwen2.5-VL-based LinMU models.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds window-size ablations in Table 4 and measured vision-encoder latencies in Table 7.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithms 1–2 and the training objectives are unchanged. v1 already leaves the vision encoder untouched; v2's decoder-specific wording clarifies the existing architecture rather than changing it.

E1.justification: The training datasets and six evaluation benchmarks in Section 4.1 are unchanged. The added ablations and timing measurements remain within the existing video-understanding and inference-efficiency coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds reported comparisons with VL-Mamba, VisualRWKV-HM (ViRWKV-HM in the table), LongLLaVA, LongVU and VAMBA. This substantially expands comparison coverage to alternative efficient VLMs, beyond the previously tabulated Transformer baselines and teacher.

E3.justification: v2 adds Stage-2 window-size evaluations at 32K tokens and isolated encoder timing on one H100. Figures 6–7 revise the stated resolution from 256×256 to 224×224; Figure 6 also changes spatial compression from 16×16 to 14×14. Reruns are not established, and Figure 7's accompanying paragraph still says 256px.

E4.justification: v2 adds spatial and temporal window-size sensitivity analysis, vision-encoder latency scaling, and a training-cost comparison. These supplement the retained distillation-stage, loss, branch-removal and backbone analyses without replacing their questions or findings.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests for its experiments. The additional results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores, ablation scores and efficiency curves are retained. v2 adds comparator scores in Table 1, additional window-configuration results in Table 4, encoder latencies ranging from 0.2694 to 2.137 seconds for 32–256 frames in Table 7, and training-cost estimates.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, state-space recurrences, losses and complexity derivations in Section 3 are unchanged. The added encoder discussion qualifies applicability without introducing a new formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows linear complexity and replacement of every self-attention layer from the entire VLM in v1 to the language-model decoder in v2. This materially limits the central architectural claim, although the accuracy and speedup claims remain unchanged and broader wording persists in the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v1 already discloses the unchanged vision encoder and excludes its latency from decoder measurements. v2 develops the implications in Section 5: possible quadratic encoder attention, effects on TTFT versus token throughput, and future encoder conversion. It also adds interpretations of window-size tradeoffs, measured encoder scaling and training-cost savings.

D1.justification: Figure 7 newly maps 128/256/512 frames to 16K/32K/64K tokens, and the new experiments specify window configurations and timing conditions. Section 4.4 adds an H100 cost equivalent; its 400 A100-hours restates the existing eight-GPU, 50-hour disclosure. The training recipe and code/data access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to VisualRWKV-HM, LongLLaVA, LongVU and VAMBA alongside their quantitative comparisons. VL-Mamba was already cited in v1. The related-work discussion and broader research positioning otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a window-ablation paragraph, Section 4.4 on training cost, Section 5 on limitations and publication front matter. Abstract and comparison passages receive targeted edits, while most prose and the methodological organization are retained; the conclusion becomes Section 6.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains rows and three model-group headings; Tables 4 and 7 are new. Existing branch and Qwen comparison tables are renumbered and relocated, Figure 7 moves, and efficiency captions are revised. Journal headers are added, but the existing figure graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The relevant efficient-model comparisons, window sensitivity results and encoder measurements modestly strengthen the evidence, while the abstract better identifies the decoder-only scope. The improvement remains limited by broader whole-model wording elsewhere, Figure 7's conflicting resolution descriptions, and Section 4.4's overstated cost-saving range: its stated NVILA costs imply about 37× savings, below the claimed 100–1000×.
